predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: Anatolia and Eastern Thrace, the last Ottoman shape: 'On 1 November 1922, the Turkish Parliament in Ankara formally abolished the Sultanate'

ledger.x: 29 October 1923: Atatürk proclaims the Republic of Turkey at Ankara.
6 August 1924: Lausanne takes effect and Karaagac is Turkish.
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: August 1974: the second operation ends in the Turkish zone.

13 February 1975: Turkey declares the occupied area a 'Federated Turkish State', the forerunner of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (independence declared in 1983, 'Turkey is the only country that recognises it').
20 January 2018: Operation Olive Branch takes Afrin.

wars.name: Turkish invasion of Cyprus
wars.outcome: Turkish victory: Turkish forces took about 36-37% of the island in two operations (20 July and 14 August 1974) and have occupied it since; the Turkish Cypriot state was declared on 13 February 1975 and again in 1983.

wars.name: Turkish military operations in northern Syria
wars.outcome: Turkey and the Syrian National Army hold the Euphrates Shield (2,225 km2), Afrin (2018) and Peace Spring (3,412-4,220 km2) zones as occupied land; the infobox runs the occupation to 2025.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed on 24 July 1923 but took effect on 6 August 1924; the Mosul frontier was still open.
Frontiers fixed by the 1921 Ankara agreement and Lausanne, and the 1939 Hatay annexation; the Turkish-Iraqi frontier of Mosul was left to the League of Nations and was not read.
